standard_prerequisites.name: A morphism of schemes is dominant if and only if its image is dense, so a morphism fails to be dominant exactly when its image is contained in a proper closed subset
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the notion is used in the counted statement at line 1336 and in the counted proof at lines 1342-1343
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the form of the hypothesis and the shape of the contradiction argument: not dominant means the image lies in a closed subset B different from S'.

standard_prerequisites.name: Fibre products of schemes and the universal property of the base change, in the form that points of a fibre product over a field-valued point are pairs of points with the same image
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof at lines 1346-1350, where the base is changed to W = Spec(kappa(f(x)))
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives that X_W and (S' minus B)_W nonempty forces their fibre product over W to be nonempty, which is the contradiction that closes the proof.

core_obligations: Set up the contradiction: assume f' is not dominant, so its image is contained in a closed subset B of S' with B different from S', and put U = S' minus B, an open nonempty subset (proof lines 1342-1343).
Push the open set down: since g is open, g(U) is a nonempty open subset of S, and since f(X) is dense in S one may choose a point x of X whose image f(x) lies in g(U) (proof lines 1344-1345).
Change the base to the spectrum W of the residue field of f(x), writing X_W, S_W and S'_W for the pullbacks of X, S and S' to W, and observe that X_W and U_W are nonempty (proof lines 1346-1348).

Conclude: over the spectrum of a field W, nonempty factors have nonempty fibre product, so X_W times_W U_W is nonempty; a point of it is a point of X times_S S' mapping into U, contradicting that f'(X times_S S') is contained in B (proof lines 1349-1351).
proof_roadmap: Assume the base change is not dominant and take a proper closed subset B of S' containing its image (proof lines 1342-1343).

Use openness of g and density of f(X) to reach the open complement of B over a residue field, then contradict the containment by producing a point of the base change over that field (proof lines 1344-1351).
difficulty_reason: The claim is that for a dominant f : X -> S and an open g : S' -> S, the base change f' : X times_S S' -> S' is again dominant (statement lines 1336-1338). The proof is a contradiction that has to move between three levels: it assumes f' is not dominant so that its image lies in a proper closed B, passes to the nonempty open U = S' minus B, uses openness of g together with density of f(X) to find x in X with f(x) in g(U), and then changes the base to W = Spec(kappa(f(x))). The step that carries the content is the last one: over the spectrum of a field the two nonempty pullbacks X_W and U_W must have a nonempty fibre product, which yields a point of X times_S S' landing in U and contradicts the containment in B (proof lines 1346-1351). This is H2: the argument is short and uses no hypothesis beyond dominance and openness, but the residue-field base change and the nonemptiness of a fibre product over a field are the non-formal moves, and neither is merely a citation in the author's text.
